blocks.content: The interior of the Earth is studied mainly through indirect scientific methods because direct observation is limited to a very small depth. The structure of the Earth's interior explains earthquakes, volcanoes, mountain building, plate tectonics, continental drift, and magnetic field generation.
The interior of the Earth is studied mainly through indirect scientific methods because direct observation is limited to a very small depth.

items: Note that indirect scientific methods (e.g., seismic waves) are critical for studying the Earth's interior as direct observation is limited.
Core geological processes tested in exams—such as magnetic field generation, continental drift, and plate tectonics—are directly driven by Earth's interior structure.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Earth's interior is primarily investigated using indirect scientific methods due to depth constraints.
Direct human observation of the interior is limited to a very small depth.
Earth's interior structure provides the explanation for seismic events (earthquakes) and volcanic activity.
Large-scale geological phenomena such as mountain building, plate tectonics, and continental drift originate from interior dynamics.
The generation of the Earth's protective magnetic field is governed by its internal structure.
